subtopics.title: Labelling Triangles and the Area Rule

questions.question: In triangle ABC, side a is always:
options: The longest side
Opposite angle A
Adjacent to angle A
The base of the triangle

questions.question: The area rule ½ab·sinC requires C to be:
options: The largest angle of the triangle
A right angle
The angle included between sides a and b
Opposite the longest side

questions.question: In triangle PQR, PQ = 7 cm, QR = 9 cm and angle Q = 50°. The area is:
In the proof of the area rule, the perpendicular height dropped onto side b equals:
options: a·sinC
b·sinC
a·cosC
c·sinB

subtopics.title: Proving and Using the Sine Rule

questions.question: The sine rule is proved by:
options: Applying Pythagoras to two right-angled triangles
Squaring both sides of the area rule
Setting the three versions of the area rule equal and dividing by ½abc
Substituting sinA = cosB into the area rule

questions.question: To use the sine rule you must know at least:
options: One side and its opposite angle, plus one more piece of information
All three sides
Two sides and the included angle
Any two angles only

questions.question: When the unknown is a SIDE, the sine rule is best written with:
options: The sines on top
The sides on top
Both sides squared
The angles in radians

questions.question: In triangle ABC, A = 40°, B = 65° and b = 12 cm. Side a equals:

subtopics.title: Finding Angles with the Sine Rule

questions.question: In triangle ABC, a = 10, b = 7 and A = 42°. Then sinB equals:
With sinB = 0,4684, angle B to one decimal place is:
A second candidate angle always exists when using inverse sine because:
options: The calculator works in radians by default
Sine is negative in the second quadrant
Cosine of the angle could also be positive
Sine is positive in both the first and second quadrants, so 180° minus the answer has the same sine

questions.question: Here the candidate B = 152,07° is rejected because:
options: It is bigger than angle A
Inverse sine can never give an obtuse angle
152,07° + 42° already exceeds 180°, so no triangle can contain both angles
Sine of 152,07° is negative

subtopics.title: Multi-Step Problems — Chaining the Two Rules

questions.question: In triangle ABC with A = 52° and B = 63°, angle C equals:
The area rule could not be used immediately in this problem because:
options: Only one side was known, and the rule needs two sides with the included angle
The triangle had no right angle
The angles did not add up to 180°
The included angle was obtuse

questions.question: With c = 15 cm and C = 65°, the sine rule gives side a as 15·sin52°/sin65°, which equals:
For the final area step using sides a and c, the included angle is B because:
options: B is the largest of the three angles
Sides a and c meet at vertex B
B was given in the question
The rule always uses the middle letter

questions.question: In the security-gate picture, sine of the included angle plays the role of:
options: The length of the longer arm
The perimeter of the cell
The squash factor that scales the area
The number of cells in the gate

questions.question: The trapped area is at its maximum when the two arms stand at:
options: 90°, where sine equals 1
180°, where the arms lie flat
45°, halfway open
60°, where sine equals a half

questions.question: At an included angle of 0° or 180° the formula gives zero area because:
options: The sides shrink to zero length
The calculator cannot evaluate those angles
The triangle becomes a circle
The arms lie flat and no triangle remains — sine of those angles is 0

questions.question: Using an angle that is NOT between the two given sides is compared to:
options: Painting the gate instead of opening it
Measuring the squash of a different cell of the gate
Oiling the wrong hinge
Counting the arms instead of the cells

subtopics.title: Fair Trade at the Triangle Market

questions.question: The market picture of the sine rule says every triangle keeps one fixed:
options: Perimeter for all three sides
Height from every vertex
Sum of the sides
Exchange rate — side over sine of its opposite angle is the same all around

questions.question: Before the sine rule can be used, the rate must be fixed by:
options: One complete pair — a side together with its opposite angle
Knowing all three angles
Measuring the longest side
Two sides and the included angle

questions.question: The writing-down trick recommended for the sine rule is:
options: Always write the sides on top no matter what
Always convert angles to radians first
Put the unknown quantity on top of the fraction
Cross-multiply before substituting values

questions.question: The 'second suspect' when finding an angle from its sine is:
options: The complement, 90° minus the calculator's answer
180° minus the calculator's answer, which has the same sine
The negative of the calculator's answer
360° minus the calculator's answer

subtopics.title: Planning the Route Before You Drive

questions.question: Multi-step problems should be planned:
options: By calculating every possible value and choosing later
Starting from the area formula and guessing
Only after finding all three sides
Backwards from what the final formula needs, before any calculation

questions.question: The 'free angle' in a triangle problem comes from:
options: The angle sum — the three angles always total 180°
The sine rule applied twice
Measuring the sketch with a protractor
Assuming the triangle is isosceles

questions.question: In the worked route, the sine rule was needed before the area rule because:
options: The sine rule is always used first in every problem
The area rule only works with whole numbers
The area rule needed a second side that was not yet known
The triangle was right-angled

questions.question: You should re-sketch and re-label the triangle even when a diagram is given because:
options: Examiners award marks for neat diagrams
Your own small-letter-opposite-capital labels make the formulae safe to apply
The given diagram is usually drawn wrongly
It uses up spare examination time
